motion: This house would ban cars from city centres

speaker: A
text: Thank you. Air pollution causes around 40,000 early deaths a year in the UK, and road traffic is the biggest single source in our cities.

speaker: A
text: When Ghent restricted cars in its centre in 2017, footfall actually went up, according to the council's own report.

speaker: B
text: That 40,000 figure is a modelled estimate from 2016, not a count of actual deaths.

speaker: B
text: And banning cars would devastate the small businesses that rely on deliveries and passing trade.

speaker: B
text: Nearly 70 percent of shoppers on our high streets arrive by car.

speaker: A
text: Small businesses would actually benefit, because pedestrians spend more per month in local shops than drivers do.

speaker: A
text: London's ultra low emission zone cut roadside nitrogen dioxide by nearly half in central London.

speaker: B
text: Honestly, I just think people should be free to choose how they travel.

speaker: B
text: Public transport in most UK cities is simply too unreliable to replace the car.

speaker: A
text: The government's own figures show bus use outside London has fallen by a third since 2010.

speaker: A
text: So the answer is to invest in buses, not to keep clogging our centres with cars.

speaker: B
text: Can I just finish my point? Electric cars will make the whole pollution argument irrelevant within ten years.
